summary: Round r1 (restricted network; data hosts blocked; one WebSearch used, which located only news/trade-press locators for the October 2024 Nepal-India-Bangladesh tripartite power sales agreement). All arrangements here are HYPOTHETICAL and do not represent any government's position or intentions. Q1 (payoff structure under a hypothetical long-term power-purchase arrangement) is answered structurally: HA-1 specifies parametric payoffs for a Nepal-side seller, the Nepal national-value stance and an Indian offtaker in terms of the 22E/22B parameters (P_EXP, P_IEX, C_TRD, C_TX_IN, C_TX_NP, P_IMP, OC_t regimes, FX_INR) plus contract variables (p_c, q_t, tenor, damages, charge allocation), with ten incentive-compatibility conditions: participation, a feasible price band, no-diversion and no-walkaway damages, approval-validity vs tenor, capacity, eligibility, ratification and currency. Variants cover seasonal energy banking (HA-2), trilateral wheeling to Bangladesh (HA-3), a jointly owned interconnector (HA-4) and a transit-service arrangement (HA-5). Documented constraints are tied to 46 source leads (Indian MoP/CEA/CERC instruments, IEX/CERC price data, NEA/ERC/NRB, the 2014 bilateral power agreement, Nepal Treaty Act and Constitution, transit texts); nearly all are reused from 22B, 22E, 17A, 17C and 27A. Every empirical item is pending; no numbers are recorded and no payoff is simulated.

findings.claim: Method: every arrangement in this file is HYPOTHETICAL; no model represents or predicts the actual position, preferences, bargaining power or intentions of any government or utility.

Method: payoffs use the 22E opportunity-cost regimes (spill, export-marginal, import-marginal) as Nepal's outside option; generation cost cancels at national level but NEA's PPA acquisition cost enters the seller's payoff.
Method: approval lapse is represented as a state variable evaluated in both states; no probability of lapse or renewal is assigned without evidence.
Method: surplus division uses generalised Nash bargaining with the weight reported only as bounds (0, 1/2, 1); the weight is not estimated or attributed.
Method: incentive compatibility is checked on block-level (15-minute/hourly aggregated to time-of-day) price distributions by Nepali month, not on monthly or annual means.

data_gaps: All 22B/22E price and cost parameters at block level by Nepali month (none retrieved in r1).
Text of the January 2024 long-term power trade agreement and the Supreme Court verdict on its ratification route (27A AR-06).
CEA DA approval orders with validity windows and renewal criteria; amendment texts of the 2018 Guidelines (eligibility clauses).
Consolidated CERC CBTE charges and NVVN trading margin applicable to Nepal schedules and to trilateral wheeling.
ERC-approved IPP PPA purchase rates by season (NEA acquisition cost C_PPA_t).
Contract text and delivery records of the October 2024 NEA-NVVN-BPDB tripartite agreement; Bangladesh buyer's alternative procurement cost (BPDB).
JV agreements, capital cost and tariff route of the October 2025 cross-border lines.
Transit protocol fee schedules, route costs and dry-port volumes for HA-5.

assumptions.text: All arrangements are hypothetical constructions for stress-testing; party labels are generic roles, not specific institutions' positions.
Nepal's outside option per MWh is the 22E opportunity cost OC_t by regime; the Indian buyer's outside option is its alternative procurement cost P_ALT_t from 22B exchange/bilateral series.
INR-settled prices are converted at the NRB NPR/INR rate for the same month; a peg change is a scenario assumption, not a forecast.
Approval lapse/renewal is modelled as a binary state evaluated in both states; no probabilities assigned.
Bargaining weights are reported as bounds only and are never attributed to any party.
National-value evaluation nets out domestic transfers (e.g. NEA-IPP PPA payments); seller-level evaluation does not.

challenges.text: The opportunity-cost table has no parameter for NEA's acquisition cost of IPP energy under ERC-approved seasonal PPA rates (C_PPA_t). It cancels at national level but determines the seller-level participation constraint in any export contract; please add it or confirm another agent owns it.

Contract incentive-compatibility checks need block-level (time-of-day) price distributions per Nepali month and the approval validity window for each approved quantum, not only monthly means and MW totals; please retain block-level extracts and validity dates in r2.

HA-1, HA-3 and HA-4 are anchored to AR-05 (2014 agreement), AR-06 (January 2024 agreement), AR-07 (October 2025 transmission agreements) and AR-29 (trilateral); please prioritise primary text for these rows in r2, including any approval-linkage, non-discriminatory-access and dispute clauses.
The October 2024 tripartite NEA-NVVN-BPDB agreement is located only by news (27B-L34..L37); please add the contract or NEA board/annual-report record as a primary lead and a BPDB purchase-cost lead.

Add catalog ids for NVVN and POWERGRID, and verify the BPDB URL. Also note: energy.MarginalUseComparison has no contract layer (price band, damages, approval state); a small extension is needed before 27B payoffs can be computed in code.

uncertainty: Very high for r1. No parameter is retrieved, so the sign of any participation constraint is unknown. Structural uncertainty: (i) whether contract prices are compared at the Nepal border or an Indian bus changes which party bears C_TX_IN; (ii) the approval regime (validity, renewal criteria, eligibility) may dominate price terms and cannot be characterised until the texts are read; (iii) block-level price variation may make monthly-mean feasibility misleading; (iv) the reference instruments (2024 long-term agreement, 2024 tripartite contract, 2025 JV lines) are located only through news and may differ from reports. Models are hypothetical and say nothing about any government's intentions.

hypothetical_arrangement_models.label: HYPOTHETICAL - constructed by NEPAL 3T for stress-testing; not a description of any existing, proposed or intended arrangement, and not the position of any government or utility.
hypothetical_arrangement_models.question: Q1 What payoff structure would each party face under a hypothetical long-term power-purchase arrangement?
hypothetical_arrangement_models.answer_status: Structure specified (HA-1, with variants HA-2..HA-4 and transit HA-5); all parameter values pending; no payoffs simulated in r1.
hypothetical_arrangement_models.method: Parametric payoff functions per party written in the 22E/22B parameter set (NPR_per_MWh primary, INR converted at the NRB NPR/INR rate for the same month). Periods are Nepali months x time blocks classified into the 22E regimes (spill, export-marginal, import-marginal). Incentive compatibility = participation for each party against its documented outside option + no-diversion/no-walkaway conditions + physical (capacity), legal (eligibility, approval validity, ratification) feasibility. Surplus division uses generalised Nash bargaining with the bargaining weight reported as bounds only. Approval lapse is treated as a state (A_t = 0/1) evaluated in both states, with no probability assigned. Payoffs are evaluated on block-level distributions, not monthly means (22E caveat).

derived_from_22E.OC_t: opportunity cost of one MWh in Nepal in period t by 22E regime: spill -> 0; export-marginal -> ENV_t; import-marginal -> P_IMP_t + Nepal-side delivery cost

models.label: HYPOTHETICAL - constructed by NEPAL 3T for stress-testing; not a description of any existing, proposed or intended arrangement, and not the position of any government or utility.
models.name: Hypothetical long-term power-purchase arrangement (seller in Nepal, buyer in India)

parties.party: Nepal-side seller/aggregator (modelled generically as 'NS'; could be NEA reselling own or IPP energy)
Nepal national accounting stance ('NN'; national value of the MWh, per 22E)
Indian offtaker ('IB'; distribution utility or trader, modelled generically)

parties.role: constraint-setter; modelled as the approval state A_t and charge schedule, with no payoff attributed

contract_terms_as_decision_variables: delivery point (Nepal border vs Indian bus)
settlement currency (INR under peg) and indexation rule

payoff_functions.NS: U_NS = sum_t A_t * q_t * [ p_c*FX_INR - C_TX_NP - (theta_S * (C_TX_IN + C_TRD))*FX_INR - C_PPA_t ] - sum_t (1-A_t) * q_t * L_S_t ;  theta_S = share of Indian-side charges borne by the seller (contract term); L_S_t = seller loss when approval lapses (damages owed unless the approval-lapse clause excuses them, net of the salvage value OC_t of the undelivered MWh)
payoff_functions.NN: W_NN = sum_t A_t * q_t * [ p_c*FX_INR - C_TX_NP - theta_S*(C_TX_IN + C_TRD)*FX_INR - OC_t ]  (national gain relative to the 22E opportunity cost; C_PPA_t is a domestic transfer and nets out nationally)
payoff_functions.IB: U_IB = sum_t A_t * q_t * [ P_ALT_t - p_c - (1-theta_S)*(C_TX_IN + C_TRD) ] - sum_t (1-A_t) * q_t * L_B_t ;  L_B_t = buyer's replacement-cost exposure when approval lapses
payoff_functions.IR: No payoff attributed. Represented only through documented rules: eligibility (ownership/financing-origin) clauses, approval validity V_A, charges C_TX_IN, deviation settlement.

outside_options.NS: sell the same MWh on the Indian exchange under a separate approval (netback ENV_t using P_IEX_t) or to the domestic grid (T_IND pathway) - whichever 22E marks as marginal
outside_options.IB: procure at P_ALT_t (exchange segment or bilateral trader)

incentive_compatibility_conditions.condition: E_seasons[ U_NS ] >= sum_t q_t * max(ENV_spot_t, domestic sale value_t) - C_PPA_t terms, evaluated separately with A_t = 1 and with A_t lapsing at each renewal date (no probability assigned)
sum_t q_t * [ P_ALT_t - p_c - (1-theta_S)(C_TX_IN + C_TRD) ] >= 0 over the tenor, evaluated on the block-level price distribution, not monthly means

a p_c exists with p_min <= p_c <= p_max, where p_min = [OC_t + C_TX_NP]/FX_INR + theta_S*(C_TX_IN + C_TRD) (q-weighted) and p_max = P_ALT_t - (1-theta_S)*(C_TX_IN + C_TRD) (q-weighted). The band is non-empty iff q-weighted P_ALT_t - (C_TX_IN + C_TRD) >= q-weighted (OC_t + C_TX_NP)/FX_INR. In spill-regime months OC_t = 0, so the Nepal-side floor is transmission cost only.
seller must not gain by diverting contracted MWh to spot in high-price blocks: d_S >= max_t( ENV_spot_t/FX_INR - p_c + theta_S-adjusted charges ) for blocks where spot netback exceeds p_c
buyer must not gain by curtailing offtake when spot is below contract: d_B >= max_t( p_c - P_ALT_t ) for blocks where P_ALT_t < p_c (take-or-pay floor)

contract value is conditional on A_t; unless the approval validity V_A covers T or renewal criteria are text-specified, both parties' participation must hold in the state where A_t lapses at the first renewal date. Tenor mismatch (T > V_A) is the key documented source of non-credibility to be tested from the DA procedure text.
sum of contracted q_t per block <= min(Cap_X, approved quantum) net of other committed flows (22E Q_CAP); otherwise the contract is physically infeasible regardless of prices
the generating assets allocated to the contract satisfy the eligibility/ownership conditions of the 2018 Guidelines as amended (04C CM-01); if not, the arrangement is infeasible for those assets

if the arrangement falls within the Nepal Treaty Act / constitutional category requiring parliamentary ratification (natural-resource sharing), ratification is a precondition; the route is documented only by the Supreme Court verdict (text pending)
INR settlement under an unchanged NPR-INR peg makes p_c*FX_INR stable in NPR; a peg change is a scenario assumption that shifts NS/NN payoffs by the change in FX_INR

models.bargaining_representation: Generalised Nash bargaining over p_c within the feasible band: maximise (U_NS - D_NS)^alpha * (U_IB - D_IB)^(1-alpha), D = outside options. alpha is NOT estimated and not attributed to any government; results are reported as the full band plus alpha in {0, 1/2, 1} as bounds, to show how surplus division moves with bargaining power.

models.name: Hypothetical seasonal energy-banking (wet-season delivery against dry-season return)
models.question_answered: Q1 (variant of a long-term arrangement without cash price)

payoff_functions.NS: U_NS = sum_wet q_w * [ -OC_w - C_TX_NP ] + sum_dry beta*q_w_alloc_d * [ P_IMP_d - C_TX_NP ]  (value of avoided dry-season imports minus wet-season opportunity cost; charges as allocated)
payoff_functions.IB: U_IB = sum_wet q_w * [ P_ALT_w - C_TX_IN_w ] - sum_dry beta*q_w_alloc_d * [ C_DRY_IN_d + C_TX_IN_d ]

incentive_compatibility_conditions.condition: beta >= (q-weighted OC_w + C_TX_NP) / (q-weighted P_IMP_d - C_TX_NP). In spill months OC_w = 0, so any beta above the charge-only floor is acceptable to NS.
beta <= (q-weighted P_ALT_w - C_TX_IN_w) / (q-weighted C_DRY_IN_d + C_TX_IN_d)

arrangement feasible iff the NS floor <= the IB ceiling; i.e. iff the wet/dry value ratio for NS is at most the wet/dry value ratio for IB. Because both parties' dry-season values reference Indian dry-season block prices, feasibility depends mainly on (i) whether Nepal's wet surplus is in spill regime and (ii) the wet-block P_ALT_w relative to dry-block prices - both pending from 22B/22E.

return obligation falls in the counterparty's high-price season; credible only if return is scheduled under an approval with validity spanning both seasons (A_t for both legs) or secured by a cash-settlement fallback at a stated index
wet-leg and dry-leg flows each within Cap_X and approved quanta in their blocks

documented_constraints.constraint: Import approvals for India-to-Nepal supply are hour-limited and time-bound (to verify from order)
Charges applicable to each leg
Dry-season import cost and wet-season spill

models.name: Hypothetical expanded trilateral sale (Nepal seller, Bangladesh buyer, wheeling through India)
models.reference_instrument: A tripartite NEA-NVVN-BPDB power sales agreement signed October 2024 is reported by news locators (27B-L34..L37); its terms are NOT used here until the contract is retrieved. HA-3 is a generic hypothetical, not a model of that contract.

payoff_functions.NS: U_NS = sum_t A_t * q_t * [ p_B*FX - C_TX_NP - theta_S*w*FX_INR - C_PPA_t ]  (FX = NPR per unit of the contract currency)
payoff_functions.BB: U_BB = sum_t A_t * q_t * [ P_ALT_BD_t - p_B - (1-theta_S)*w_conv - C_TX_BD ]  (C_TX_BD = Bangladesh-side delivery cost, pending)
payoff_functions.IT: U_IT = sum_t A_t * q_t * [ w - c_IT_t ]  where c_IT_t = losses cost + congestion opportunity cost of the corridor capacity in block t (value of the same capacity for Indian own trades, proxied by the block price spread) - pending

incentive_compatibility_conditions.condition: p_B net of w and Nepal-side cost >= Nepal's best alternative for the same MWh (ENV_t on the Indian exchange if approved, else OC_t)
P_ALT_BD_t >= p_B + delivery and wheeling cost borne by BB
w >= c_IT_t in every scheduled block; if the corridor is congested in Nepal's wet season, c_IT_t rises and the approval state A_t is the operative constraint

a (p_B, w) pair satisfying all three exists iff q-weighted P_ALT_BD_t - C_TX_BD - c_IT_t >= q-weighted OC_t + C_TX_NP (all converted at same-period rates). Surplus split is a three-party bargaining problem; no split is attributed to any party.

requires Indian DA approval for trade between two neighbouring countries through India; the reported June 2026 withholding of an extension (news locator only) shows A_t can be 0 for expansion tranches - to verify from the primary order

documented_constraints.constraint: Provisions for trade between neighbouring countries via the Indian grid
Trading agency margin and role

Approval status for extension

models.name: Hypothetical shared cross-border transmission (jointly owned interconnector with cost and capacity-rent sharing)
models.question_answered: supporting Q1: the physical precondition for HA-1..HA-3
models.reference_instrument: October 2025 NEA-POWERGRID JV agreements reported by news locator (27B-L31; 27A AR-07). Their ownership shares and tariff route are unverified and not used.

payoff_functions.NX: U_NX = s_N * ( R_X - OM_X ) - s_N * K_X * CRF + B_N ;  B_N = sum_t Q_trade_t(Cap_X, A_t) * [ ENV_t - OC_t ]^+ + import-reliability value (dry-season P_IMP savings vs unserved energy cost, pending from 05B)
payoff_functions.IX: U_IX = (1 - s_N) * ( R_X - OM_X ) - (1 - s_N) * K_X * CRF + B_I ;  B_I = sum_t Q_trade_t * [ P_ALT_t - p_c ]^+ (buyer-side gains) + system benefits (not attributed without evidence)
payoff_functions.R_X: regulated line revenue = allowed transmission tariff (ERC/CERC determination, pending) x usage; or capacity rent = flow x cross-border price difference if merchant (hypothetical variant)

incentive_compatibility_conditions.condition: B_N + B_I + R_X >= K_X*CRF + OM_X (line is worth building jointly)

cost share s_N lies in [ (K_X*CRF + OM_X - R_X - B_I)/(K_X*CRF + OM_X - R_X), B_N/(K_X*CRF + OM_X - R_X) ] when K_X*CRF + OM_X > R_X (core of the two-party cost game); empty if B_N or B_I is too small

B_N depends on A_t and approved quanta, which are set unilaterally and for shorter periods than line life. Nepal-side participation is robust only if IC4-individual holds when B_N is evaluated with Q_trade limited to currently approved quanta, or if approval of trade over the line is contractually linked to capacity (clause to look for in the 2014 agreement and JV texts)

parties.party: Transit state authorities and operators ('TS'; generic)

payoff_functions.NT: U_NT = sum_r V_r * [ c_ref - c_r - f_r - tau_r * h ]  (V_r volume on route r; c_ref cost on the reference route; c_r route cost; f_r transit fees/charges; tau_r transit time; h value of time per unit cargo)
payoff_functions.TS: U_TS = sum_r V_r * [ f_r + m_r - a_r - e_r ]  (m_r operator margin on port/rail services; a_r administration/security cost; e_r expected enforcement cost of diversion into the domestic market - modelled as a documented-procedure cost, not a probability)

incentive_compatibility_conditions.condition: c_r + f_r + tau_r*h <= c_ref for a route to attract volume
f_r + m_r >= a_r + e_r per unit

a fee f_r exists iff c_ref - c_r - tau_r*h >= a_r + e_r - m_r; sealing/guarantee procedures lower e_r but raise c_r and tau_r - the trade-off to be measured from procedure texts and dry-port statistics
